It claims 1 trillion total parameters with roughly 50 billion active parameters per forward pass, consistent with a mixtureofexpertsstyle description.[3]

 What that means

“1T parameters” describes the model’s total stored parameter capacity; “50B active” means only a subset is used for a typical inference pass. In principle, that can reduce compute relative to a dense onetrillionparameter model, while preserving high overall capacity.

The model card’s stated provenance matters: it says the architecture and pretrained weights originate from the underlying OpenModel1TA50BInstruct base, and that the Omega branding does not mean Omega originally trained those weights.[3]

 Practical caveat

Those figures are publisherprovided modelcard claims. Before deploying it, verify that the repository includes actual weight files, a clear license, configuration/tokenizer assets, reproducible evaluation details, and hardware/runtime requirements—not merely metadata or a redirecting derivative page. Hugging Face is a hosting and collaboration platform, not an automatic independent validation of every model’s stated capabilities.[2]

If you share what you want to do with it—local inference, API serving, finetuning, or assessing whether the model claim is credible—I can help evaluate the appropriate next steps.
